chunks: Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who played with water, rinsing his mouth with it due to thirst, and it entered his throat. He said:
"He must make it up. But if it was during wudu (ablution), there is no harm in it."

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Does swallowing water accidentally while rinsing the mouth break the fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a fasting person whose mouth-rinsing causes water to enter the throat. If it happened while rinsing due to thirst, the fast must be made up; but if it occurred during wudu (ablution), there is no blame.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1867 - Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who played with water by rinsing his mouth due to thirst, and it entered his throat.
Imam (as) said: "He must make up his fast. However, if it was during ablution (wudu), there is no harm in it."
